title: Priv EKS control-plane terraform assembly: upgrade hooks, preflight probes, and runtime health harness
creator: Maya Patel
description: Deliver a hardened Terraform module (module.redwood/priv-eks-controlplane) that automates EKS control-plane provisioning for Private deployments with opinionated defaults for network isolation, KMS-integrated secrets, and safe upgrade hooks. Scope: idempotent creation, preflight validations, canary upgrade choreography, canary-to-rolling promotion policy, runtime liveness & readiness probes exposed to Redwood Console, and integration points for Audit Logging and KMS. This ticket covers module design, CI plan, basic docs, and initial canary rollout runbook.
acceptance_criteria: Module can create and tear down control-plane resources idempotently across repeat runs
Preflight validations fail fast with clear error codes when VPC/subnet/KMS perms are missing
Upgrade path supports canary nodegroup update with automated health gating and rollback on failed probes
Health harness emits metrics to Prometheus (controlplane_health_check{phase}) and logs to S3/audit sink for failed upgrades
Terraform plan/apply CI pipeline that runs plan in staging and blocks on health gates before production apply
design_decisions: Use a small, opinionated set of input variables to reduce user error and default to customer-owned KMS when provided
Separate 'control-plane' and 'control-plane-shared' resources to allow identical blueprints across accounts while minimizing cross-account state
Implement a preflight module that can be invoked independently to verify IAM/KMS/VPC prerequisites before main apply
Leverage SSM Parameter Store for storing last-successful-upgrade version tag for safe rollbacks
implementation_notes: Using EKS eksctl-style module was rejected due to lack of fine-grained IAM control; we implemented native aws_eks_cluster + aws_eks_node_group resources
KV cache for rollout state implemented via DynamoDB with conditional writes to avoid race conditions across CI runners
Added a lightweight lambda health-prober used during canary phases to exercise control-plane endpoints and emit structured results to CloudWatch logs

2026-03-06: Implemented canary update workflow using DynamoDB coordination and Lambda prober; early tests show 90s median verification latency
2026-03-10: Security review kickoff with Security team; identified need to avoid storing plaintext credentials in state and to add additional KMS key policy checks
2026-03-12: PR #7632 opened for internal review; reviewers: Ayumi Tanaka (Infra), Jorge Mendez (Security), Priya Rao (Platform)
2026-03-14: Addressed reviewer feedback: added explicit kms:Decrypt guardrails, tightened IAM policies, and added optional HSM hook for customers with FIPS/HSM requirements
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: In-place upgrades could cause control-plane downtime if preflight misses edge cases; Mitigation: require canary promotion and automatic rollback on probe failures

Risk: Terraform state exposure of sensitive outputs; Mitigation: mark sensitive values, avoid storing secrets in state, integrate with remote state encryption, and require KMS key ownership or grant binding
Risk: Cross-account role assumption failure for enterprise customers; Mitigation: provide a documented role-assumption scaffold and a validation step in preflight
testing_plan: Unit tests for validation logic (preflight) using terratest harness
E2E staging pipeline that performs create -> apply -> canary upgrade -> promotion -> rollback scenarios
Chaos test: simulate API throttling during upgrade to verify rollback triggers
Security tests: IAM policy lint, KMS policy smoke, and secret exposure scan
